concepts.name: selling the sausage approach
concepts.definition: A marketing style that focuses on promoting the appealing aspects of a product or idea rather than the product itself; applied to environmental issues, it is criticized for failing to deliver the fundamental changes needed to stay within ecological limits.
concepts.supporting_text: In the 1940s, US salesman Elmer Wheeler advised businesses on his 'Don't sell the sausage, sell the sizzle!' marketing approach... there is increasing recognition that the 'selling the sausage' approach to environmental issues is not delivering the fundamental changes required to stay within ecological limits.

significance.justification: Identified as a marketing tactic that fails to deliver the fundamental changes needed for ecological limits.
significance.supporting_text: There is increasing recognition that the ‘selling the sausage’ approach to environmental issues is not delivering the fundamental changes required to stay within ecological limits.

concepts.name: green heaven
concepts.definition: A positive, appealing vision of a greener future that frames sustainable behaviour as a desirable, high‑quality way of life, intended to win hearts and minds for a transition to a low‑carbon society.
concepts.supporting_text: The challenge of the environmental movement is to communicate a vision that sells a 'green heaven'; one that puts the sizzle back into green behaviour and demonstrates that a transition to a low-carbon society ultimately means a better quality of life for everyone.

significance.justification: Proposed as an appealing vision to win hearts and minds, enhancing public acceptance of greener lifestyles.
significance.supporting_text: The challenge of the environmental movement is to communicate a vision that sells a ‘green heaven’; ... demonstrates that a transition to a low‑carbon society ultimately means a better quality of life for everyone.

concepts.name: value‑action gap
concepts.definition: The inconsistency where individuals' expressed green attitudes or values do not translate into corresponding environmentally friendly actions.
concepts.supporting_text: This inconsistent 'value-action' gap is where attitudes to green behaviour differ from actual behaviour.

significance.justification: Highlights the persistent mismatch between green attitudes and actual behaviour, a barrier to harmony with nature.
significance.supporting_text: This inconsistent ‘value–action’ gap is where attitudes to green behaviour differ from actual behaviour.

concepts.name: low‑carbon society
concepts.definition: A societal state characterized by reduced carbon emissions, presented as leading to a better quality of life for everyone.
concepts.supporting_text: demonstrates that a transition to a low-carbon society ultimately means a better quality of life for everyone.

significance.justification: Represents the systemic transition needed for sustainable human‑nature interdependence.
significance.supporting_text: …demonstrates that a transition to a low‑carbon society ultimately means a better quality of life for everyone.

concepts.name: green lifestyle
concepts.definition: A way of living that is perceived as environmentally friendly, encompassing everyday activities that have an impact on the planet; the text notes that many people believe they already live green lifestyles and that for broader adoption it must be easier, more convenient, and cheaper.
concepts.supporting_text: This confusion about what a green lifestyle actually entails is evident in the responses to a 2009 UK survey on the issue. A green lifestyle was no longer seen as an alternative lifestyle by half of the respondents... While there is a willingness to undertake green actions that are easy, such as recycling or switching off lights, there is often a reluctance to change behaviour with regard to car use, long-haul holidays and the purchase of goods. ... A greener lifestyle has to be an easier, convenient and cheaper option for everyone if people are to be encouraged to think about their impact on the planet.

significance.justification: The text highlights widespread misunderstanding of what a green lifestyle entails.
significance.supporting_text: A green lifestyle was no longer seen as an alternative lifestyle by half of the respondents
